test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 18 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What will be the difference in population 3 years ago and 2 years ago of a town whose current population of 2,50,000 is increasing at a rate of 25% every year?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Fractional rate** of 25% = 1/4. Population **increases** from 4 to 5 each year.

Let population 3 years ago be P. Then 2 years ago, it was P × (5/4). Current population = P × (5/4)³.

P × (125/64) = 2,50,000 ⇒ P = 1,28,000.

Difference = (Population 2 years ago) − (Population 3 years ago) = P × (5/4 − 1) = P × 1/4.

Difference = 1,28,000 ÷ 4 = 32,000.

**∴ The correct answer is 32,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Current Population = 2,50,000; Rate (R) = 25% per annum; Time (n) = 3 years.

**Formula Used:** Population n years ago = P / (1 + R/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/57b6538d6fb151097fddc667a146bfd3b03b651191e7a0a7467fd3e7c140594e.png] 

⇒ Population 3 years ago = 2,50,000 / (1 + 25/100)³

⇒ Population 3 years ago = 2,50,000 / (5/4)³ = 2,50,000 × (64/125) = 1,28,000

⇒ Population 2 years ago = (Population 3 years ago) × (1 + 25/100)

⇒ Population 2 years ago = 1,28,000 × 1.25 = 1,60,000

⇒ Required Difference = 1,60,000 − 1,28,000 = 32,000

**∴ The correct answer is 32,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Population Growth Formula

Future Population = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ, where P is initial population, R is growth rate, and n is time.

Population Decrease Formula

If population decreases, use P(1 − R/100)ⁿ. This is similar to the **Depreciation** formula in accounting.

Successive Percentage Change

For two years with different rates R₁ and R₂, the final population is P(1 + R₁/100)(1 + R₂/100).</p
